settings.uses:
A demo of the optional setup notes. Markdown works here: **bold**, `code`,
and lists.

- Workbench: oak, scarred, third-hand
- Familiar: a moth who judges silently
settings.body: A record from a world that does not exist. Every entry in this demo names the feature or edge case it exercises; replace all of it with your own life.

experience.title: Guild Artificer
experience.body:
- The current post: no `endDate`, so the range renders as "Present".
- `employmentType` is set, so the badge appears next to the title.
- Bullet-point bodies render as the responsibility list.

experience.title: Foundry Enchanter
experience.body:
- A finished engagement: both dates set, so the full range renders.
- `employmentType: contract` shows the type badge is not limited to full-time.
- No `link`, so the foundry's name stays plain text.

experience.title: Apprentice Tinker
experience.body: - No `employmentType` at all: the badge simply does not render, and nothing is invented in its place. The site never overclaims what the record does not say.

education.title: Magister of Aetheric Systems
education.body:
The fully-dressed degree: `gpa` and `link` are both optional and both present here, and the title already carries the field, so the duplicate field line is suppressed while the `degree` badge still renders ("Magister" and "Master" are different words). Markdown headings in the body render as sub-sections.

### Thesis · A Simulation Frame for Tidal Ley-Lines

One or two sentences describing the thesis; long-form detail belongs in a blog post linked from here.

### Selected Coursework

Distributed Wards · Numerical Divination · Systems Alchemy · Technical Calligraphy

education.title: First Circle Diploma in Artifice
education.body: The minimal degree, and an open one: `degree: Journeyman` is nobody's official credential level, yet it renders as a proper badge because degree values are open strings. No `gpa`, no `link`, so those rows hide cleanly, and the title already says "Artifice", so the duplicate field line is suppressed.

awards.title: Grand Prize of the Artificers' Fair
awards.body: A plain award with a link: the issuer renders as the subtitle and the entry links out. `awardType` groups the Awards page.

awards.title: Wyvern Regatta · First Place
awards.body: An owner-invented `awardType`. Type fields are open strings: "beast-racing" is not in any predefined list, yet it groups and labels correctly (Title Case fallback). An accomplishment ledger should never gate what counts as an accomplishment.

awards.title: The Archmage's Stipend
awards.body: A scholarship with an `amount`: the sum renders for scholarships and grants, and it is a free string, so "500 gold crowns" works as well as any currency. No `link`, so the title stays plain text.

publications.title: A Latency Atlas of the Known Realms
publications.body: A preprint: `pubType` drives the badge, and the link points at the scroll archive since there is no DOI yet.

publications.title: Scheduling Strategies for Tidal Ley-Line Grids
publications.body: The fully-dressed journal article: `doi` and `link` both render as outbound chips, and `year` drives the newest-first ordering. The site owner's name is emphasized in the author line by matching the profile name.

publications.title: Tracing Failures Across Distributed Wards
publications.body: A conference paper with no `doi` and no `link`: the chips simply do not render. The "et al." author form works when the full list is unavailable.

publications.title: Stormcaller Buoy (Charter of Invention No. 000001)
publications.body: An owner-invented `pubType`: "charter" is not a predefined value (neither was "patent"), but open type fields accept anything citable and label it correctly.

speaking.title: The Grand Conclave of Mages 2026
speaking.body: An owner-invented `speakingType`: "attendance" records being in the hall, not at the lectern, and the open type field labels it honestly. The `story` field links this entry to a long-form piece; the counts on the home page say "entries", never "talks", so attendance never overclaims.

speaking.title: Observability for Small Guilds
speaking.body: The fully-dressed talk: `link`, `slides`, and `video` each render their own outbound chip when present.

volunteering.title: Peer Reviewer
volunteering.body: Ongoing service: an empty `endDate` renders as "Present". Manuscript reviews and scholarly service live in volunteering by convention.

volunteering.title: Mentor
volunteering.body: A finished engagement with the optional `role` and `location` filled and no `link`: every optional field hides or shows independently.

certificates.title: Certified Golem Architect · Associate
certificates.body: The fully-dressed certificate: `credentialId` renders as a mono chip and `link` points at the verification sigil. `certType` feeds the filter pills on the certificates page.

certificates.title: Elvish Language Certificate · B2
certificates.body: A language certificate: `certType: language` shows the type list is open to any domain, and with no `credentialId` or `link` the chips just do not render.

certificates.title: Wilds Field Medicine
certificates.body: An owner-invented `certType`: "field-craft" is nobody's official category, and it still filters and labels correctly (Title Case fallback). Certificates are whatever you have a parchment for.

references.title: Further references
references.name: Further references
references.body: The minimal reference: just a name and a body. Available upon request.

references.title: Reference from thesis supervisor
references.name: Archmagister Rowan Halloway
references.body: The fully-dressed reference: `name` is the primary identifier (not `title`), the email renders as an obfuscated copy-chip rather than a scrapeable mailto, and the phone and profile link show when present.

interests.title: Dragon watching
interests.body: An interest with both a body and a `story` link: the ledger row shows this one-liner and the "read the story" affordance side by side. From a safe distance, always.

interests.title: Gryphon riding
interests.body: An interest with a body but no story: just the one-line voice, no link.

interests.title: Wand whittling
interests.body: An owner-invented `category`: "craft" is not in the curated order, so it appends after the known categories alphabetically. Interest categories are open strings like every type field.

organizations.title: The Artificers' Guild
organizations.body: A current membership: empty `endDate` renders as ongoing, and `website` links the card out.

organizations.title: The Cinderfen Makers' Circle
organizations.body: A past community membership: both dates set, no `website`. `memberType` is an open string like every type field.

projects.title: The Everburning Lantern
projects.body: The fully-dressed project: `featured: true` headlines the home page's Selected work chapter and the top of the projects ledger, and it carries every optional field at once (image, link, role, stats, tags). The first featured entry wins; with none, the newest project takes the spot.

projects.title: Paper Wyvern
projects.body: A project with no link at all. Link-less entries are first-class: the title renders as plain text, nothing pretends to be clickable, and the entry still opens its detail modal.

projects.title: Tidewarden's Gauge
projects.body: A linked project without an image: the ledger renders a quiet glyph placeholder instead of leaving a hole, and the title links out with a host chip.

projects.title: Grimoire of Field Notes
projects.body: The broken-image case: the `image` URL here returns nothing, so the SafeImage component swaps in its quiet glyph fallback instead of a browser error icon. Hot-linked previews that die later never break the page.

projects.title: The Undated Reliquary
projects.body: An entry with no `year`. Dated lists sort newest first, and undated entries close the list instead of poisoning the order, so this one always sits at the bottom of the ledger. Nobody remembers when the reliquary was made, which is rather the point.

posts.title: A Half-Formed Incantation
posts.desc: A Seedling note, planted before it is ready.
posts.body: A `Seedling`: the garden's youngest kind, published while still rough. The kind badge and the filter pills come straight from this frontmatter value.

posts.title: On Conjured Content
posts.desc: An Evergreen note, the settled end of the garden spectrum.
posts.body: An `Evergreen` note: revised until stable, kept because it stays true. Good demo content is documentation that happens to render; each entry in this seed states which behavior it exercises, even when the entry is about dragons.

posts.title: The Reading Ledger
posts.desc: A living list, the third of the open note kinds.
posts.body:
The `List` kind: a long living document that grows over time rather than maturing like a note. Garden kinds are open strings; Seedling and Evergreen are conventions, not a schema.

- *The Sea of Forgotten Stars* · finished, worth the hype
- *Runes & Ruination* · in progress
- *A Field Guide to Invisible Beasts* · next

blog.title: Hello, VITA
blog.excerpt: The fully-dressed native blog post, with a cover, a series, a reading time, and tags.
blog.body:
This is a native post: it lives in the repo, renders on its own route, and carries every optional field at once. The `cover` shows in the ledger and on the post page, `series` groups related posts, `readingTime` renders as a mono readout, and tags feed the blog's filter pills.

Story links from other content types (an interest, a book, a speaking entry, a city) can point at a post like this one, so a one-line record connects to real writing. Half of Wren's demo record ends up here, which is exactly the point.

## Markdown works everywhere

Bodies are Markdown: **bold**, `code`, lists, and headings all render through the shared prose styles.

blog.title: Published in Another Realm
blog.excerpt: An externally-published post; the canonical home is another realm's press and VITA links out.
blog.body: The `externalUrl` case: writing whose canonical home is elsewhere (a guild gazette, another realm's press, Medium in the mundane world) renders distinctly in every list: a dashed frame, a host chip naming the destination, and an outbound arrow. Clicking goes straight to the source; this body, if present, shows as a summary only.

blog.title: The Bare Minimum Scroll
blog.body: A post with no cover, no series, no excerpt, and no reading time: the ledger derives its preview from the body's first lines, and every missing field simply hides. Even the humblest scroll gets shelved properly.

updates.title: Untitled
updates.body: A `milestone` update: the loudest of the three feed kinds, for events worth a flag. The demo record went live across the realms today. The newest updates feed the home page's Now chapter.

updates.title: Untitled
updates.body: A `note` update: a short thought with no ceremony, the kind a familiar would ignore. The type defaults to note when omitted.

updates.title: Untitled
updates.body: A `link` update: commentary attached to a URL, with `linkTitle` naming the destination chip.

books.title: A Field Guide to Invisible Beasts
books.author: Q. Alder
books.body: A book on the To Read shelf carrying a `story` link: the modal offers "read the story", pointing at the garden's reading ledger. Any item can connect to its long-form writing this way.

books.title: Runes & Ruination
books.author: Ines Kovar
books.body: A finished book with no cover and no rating: the shelf renders a quiet placeholder spine, and the rating row hides.

books.title: The Sea of Forgotten Stars
books.author: Marlowe of the Deepward
books.body: The fully-dressed book: a cover, a status, and a rating. The library shelves order To Read, then Reading, then Read; this one sits on the middle shelf.

courses.title: Practical Scrying
courses.body: A course with a `link` and a `date`: courses render on the education page under Courses & Continued Learning, next to the formal degrees.

courses.title: Introduction to Realm Cartography
courses.body: A course without a `link`: the provider renders as plain text and nothing pretends to be clickable.

trips.title: Lanternfall
trips.body: The fully-dressed city: a date (which drives newest-first ordering and the realm's year group), an image, coordinates (a free string, so any system of navigation works), and a `story` link to long-form writing about the journey.

trips.title: Skelda
trips.body: A dated city under a realm that declares no `years` of its own: the realm's year group derives from its newest city date, so Rimeholt files under 2024 because of this entry.

trips.title: Thornwick
trips.body: The orphan case: this city names a `country` that has no realm entry of its own, so it renders under the orphan group instead of disappearing. The join is an exact string match on the realm's name; add a Verdant Wilds country file and this city moves home.

trips.title: Mistharbor
trips.body: The minimal city: no date, no image, no coordinates. Undated cities close their realm's list, and the missing image renders as the quiet glyph placeholder.

countries.title: Rimeholt
countries.name: Rimeholt
countries.body: A realm with no `years` and no image of its own: its year group derives from its newest dated city, and with none it would file under Undated, which always closes the list.

countries.title: The Sundermist Isles
countries.name: The Sundermist Isles
countries.body: The fully-dressed realm: an image, explicit `years` (which place it in the year groups), and two city entries joined to it by an exact `country` name match.
